title: A Caesar cipher
hints: Runes are integers, so you can do arithmetic on them: r - 'a' is a letter's position in the alphabet, 0 to 25. Only shift ASCII letters, keep their case, and copy everything else unchanged.
In Go, % keeps the sign of the left operand: -1 % 26 == -1. Normalize the shift first with ((shift % 26) + 26) % 26 so negative shifts work. strings.Builder's WriteRune builds the result efficiently.
k := ((shift%26)+26)%26; for each rune r: switch { case 'a' <= r && r <= 'z': r = 'a' + (r-'a'+rune(k))%26; case 'A' <= r && r <= 'Z': r = 'A' + (r-'A'+rune(k))%26 }; b.WriteRune(r)
